title: Build, Evaluate and Deploy a RAG-Based Retail Copilot with Azure AI: Cedric Vidal and David Smith
talk_summary: A hands-on Microsoft workshop building a RAG retail copilot on Azure AI Studio using prompt flow, Azure AI Search vectors, and Cosmos DB, then deploying it as an endpoint. The most transferable content is the LLM-as-judge evaluation loop (groundedness/relevance/coherence/fluency scored 0-5 by a stronger model) and the hybrid keyword+vector retrieval advice.

takeaways.what_they_do: A stronger model (GPT-4) scores the cheaper production model's answers on groundedness, relevance, coherence, and fluency on a 0-5 scale, using the question, retrieved context, and answer as inputs; scores are used to gate prompt/retrieval changes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: ask gp4 on a scale of 0 to five how relevant is this answer how grounded is this answer in the data
takeaways.numbers: 0-5 scale; adversarial toothbrush question scored groundedness 1/5, relevance 1/5, coherence 4/5, fluency 5/5

takeaways.technique: Adversarial/negative test cases in eval set
takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately include out-of-domain questions (a toothbrush at a camping store) to verify the system refuses or scores low rather than fabricating, and keep the eval set to re-run on model upgrades.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you probably also want to test out your llm on some adversarial types of responses

takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than tuning ANN parameters for recall, they combine keyword search with vector search because the combination outperforms either alone; Azure AI Search defaults to hybrid.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a combination of keyword search and Vector search together um actually outperforms either

takeaways.technique: DAG with code-in-node conditionals, not graph branching
takeaways.what_they_do: Prompt flow is a fixed DAG where every node always executes; conditionals/loops live inside a node's Python or Jinja template, not as graph edges. They explicitly say it is not a business-process orchestrator.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all the nodes in the dag are going to be executed you cannot have conditional node execution

takeaways.technique: Privileged endpoint pattern with user ID passed as parameter
takeaways.what_they_do: The web app has no DB access; it passes only a user ID and question to the endpoint, which queries the DB with a privileged account and returns only the generated text, limiting what the client can reach.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the app doesn't have any direct access to databases at all
